hints: Focus on what actually attacks the carbonyl carbon, and whether acid or base would help make more of that attacker.
Write the cyanohydrin from pentan-2-one as $\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CN)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and list the four groups on the new carbon.
Check if anything is lost or replaced in $\text{C=O} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{C(OH)(CN)}$, then decide between addition, substitution and condensation.
walkthrough:
**Recall the real reaction**

Think of this as HCN adding across the C=O double bond to make a cyanohydrin. No atoms leave, they just add on.

$$\text{R}_2\text{C=O} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C(OH)(CN)}$$

**Spot the mechanism and catalyst**

The nucleophile is $\text{CN}^-$, not HCN itself, so a trace of base such as $\text{NaCN}$ or $\text{KCN}$ catalyses it. Acid would remove $\text{CN}^-$ by forming HCN, so concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ stops the reaction.

$$\text{HCN} + \text{OH}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{CN}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Test pentan-2-one for chirality**

Pentan-2-one is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Adding HCN gives 2-hydroxy-2-methylpentanenitrile.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CN)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
The new C-2 is bonded to $\text{-OH}$, $\text{-CN}$, $\text{-CH}_3$ and $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Four different groups means a chiral centre, formed as a racemic mixture.

**Name the reaction type correctly**

Because the C=O pi bond breaks and both H and CN add with nothing lost, this is nucleophilic addition. It is not substitution (nothing is replaced) and not condensation (no water or small molecule is eliminated).

options.A: False. The active nucleophile is CN-, so the reaction needs a trace of base like NaCN. Concentrated H2SO4 would protonate CN- to HCN and destroy the nucleophile, inhibiting the reaction.
options.B: Correct. The product is CH3C(OH)(CN)CH2CH2CH3. The C-2 carbon carries four different groups: OH, CN, CH3 and CH2CH2CH3, so it is chiral and obtained as a racemic mixture.
options.C: False. A condensation reaction eliminates a small molecule such as water. Here all atoms of the carbonyl and HCN are retained in the cyanohydrin, so it is a simple addition reaction.
options.D: False. Substitution replaces one atom or group by another. Here no leaving group leaves, the C=O pi bond is broken and CN- adds to carbon followed by protonation of oxygen, which is nucleophilic addition.
